revenue increased 17% and 14% in constant currency, with consistent execution in the core
business and increasing contribution from strong Copilot results. ARPU growth was again led by
E5 and M365 Copilot, and paid M365 commercial seats grew 6% year-over-year to over $450
million, with installed base expansion across all customer segments, though primarily in our small
and medium business and frontline worker offerings.
M365 Commercial products revenue increased 13% and 10% in constant currency, ahead of
expectations due to higher than expected Office 2024 transactional purchasing. M365 consumer
cloud revenue increased 29% and 27% in constant currency, again, driven by ARPU growth. M365
Consumer subscriptions grew 6%. LinkedIn revenue increased 11% and 10% in constant currency,
driven by marketing solutions. Dynamics 365 revenue increased 19% and 17% in constant currency,
with continued growth across all workloads. Segment gross margin dollars increased 17% and 15%
in constant currency and gross margin percentage increased, again, driven by efficiency gains at
M365 commercial cloud that were partially offset by continued investments in AI, including the
impact of growing Copilot usage.
Operating expenses increased 6% and 5% in constant currency, and operating income increased
22% and 19% in constant currency. Operating margins increased year-over-year to 60%, driven by
improved operating leverage as well as the higher gross margins noted earlier. Next, the
Intelligent Cloud segment. Revenue was $32.9 billion and grew 29% and 28% in constant currency.
In Azure and other cloud services, revenue grew 39% and 38% in constant currency, slightly
ahead of expectations with ongoing efficiency gains across our fungible fleet, enabling us to
reallocate some capacity to Azure that was monetized in the quarter.
As mentioned earlier, we continue to see strong demand across workloads, customer segments,
and geographic regions, and demand continues to exceed available supply.

What We Liked / What We're watching on the Quarter
Revenue/Bookings
(+) F2Q revenue of $81.3bn was 1.5% above the midpoint of guidance, with upside 
concentrated in PBP & IC segments. On a constant currency basis, growth ticked 
down ~1.5pts sequentially to +15% y/y.
(+) Commercial Bookings rose +228% y/y @cc. This was primarily driven by the 
previously disclosed larger Azure commit from OpenAI, alongside benefit from the 
recent Anthropic commitment and "healthy growth" across core annuity sales 
motions on a lower expiry base when adjusted for OpenAI contracts in the prior 
year. Commercial RPO ended the quarter +110% y/y to $625bn; ~45% of the total 
balance is now attributed to commits from OpenAI, with the remaining core 55% 
growing +28% y/y. Total Commercial cRPO now stands at +39% y/y, up from +21% 
a year prior.
Business Lines
(=) Azure growth of +38% y/y @CC was 1pt above guidance (37%), but likely a touch 
shy of buyside expectations that we believe were closer to ~+39%. Upside to 
guidance was a result of efficiency gains across the fleet enabling reallocation of 
some capacity from other segments to monetizable Azure demand. We underscore 
that these results were once again limited by supply constraints as mgmt. noted the 
need to balance increasing Azure demand with growing needs across 1P services, 
increasing allocation to R&D teams, and replacement of end-of-life equipment.
(=) M365 Commercial Cloud growth of +14% y/y came in line with the high end of 
guidance +13-14% y/y @cc, with growth once again driven by a combination of 
seat growth (+6% y/y) and ARPU expansion. ARPU expansion also continues to be 
attributed to E5 momentum and then M365 Copilot. This quarter was also the first 
time mgmt. disclosed M365 copilot paid seats, which sit at 15m as of F2Q.
